{{nihongo|'''Mishima-Kamo Shrine'''|三島鴨神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Settsu Province]].

``Mishima Kamo Shrine'' is located in {{jalink|Osaka Prefecture|Q122723}}{{jalink|Takatsuki City|Q335423}}. In {{jalink|Shikinaisha}}{{jalink|Ronsha|Q135022904}}, {{jalink|Modern shrine rank system|Q712534|Old shrine rank}} is {{jalink|Gosha|Q134917316}}.

According to the shrine legend, it was called ``Mishima Island'' along with {{jalink|Oyamazumi Shrine|Q703904}} in {{jalink|Iyo Province|Q907829|Iyo}} and {{jalink|Mishima Taisha|Q650772}} in {{jalink|Izu Province|Q860928|Izu}}.<ref name="place name">"Place name of Osaka prefecture" Mishima Kamo Shrine section. </ref>. It is also said to be the first {{jalink|Mishima Shrine|Q11355275}} (Yamazumi Shrine) in Japan. However, before the 17th century, it was called ``Ikushima Daimyojin.''

== Enshrined God ==
The following two deities are currently enshrined <ref>[http://www.tcn.zaq.ne.jp/akbus600/keidai/honden/honden.html Precinct Guide/Main Hall] (official website). </ref>.
* '''{{jalink|Oyamatsumi|Q386563|Oyamazumi}}''' (Oyamazumi no Kami)
:: According to the Iyo no Kuni Fudoki Ibibun, <!-- "The district of Kichi. Mishima. The name of the seated god is the god of Oyamazumi, and one is the great god of Watashi. The god of Kore appeared in the shrine of Takatsu in Namba during the reign of the Emperor Ushimeshi. This god came from the country of Baekje. ``Mishima is the name of the island in Tsu-no-kuni.'': Comment out the original text for better visibility. Sekijin (same as Oyamazumi no Mikoto) is also known as ``Watashi no Okami'' and is said to have come from {{jalink|Baekje|Q28428}} during the reign of Emperor Nintoku|Q313119}} and was enshrined on the island of Tsu no Kuni. Mishimajo. </ref>.
:: "Mishima of Tsu no Kuni" means {{jalink|Settsu Province|Q864163}} Mishima (current According to this description, the deity enshrined at {{jalink|Oyamazumi Shrine|Q703904}} ({{jalink|Ehime Prefecture|Q123376}}{{jalink|Imabari City|Q461020}}) was originally a local deity.::However, Shikinaisha Mishima Kamo Shrine means ``Kamo Shrine'' located on Mishima Island, and some have pointed out that Shikinaisha Mishima Kamo Shrine and the ``Mishima of Tsu no Kuni (= Mishima God)'' that appear in the Fudoki are not the same.
* '''{{jalink|Kotoshiro nushi|Q8009611|Kotoshiro nushi kami}}''' (Kotoshironushi no Kami)
:: Kotoshironushigami is said to be the guardian deity of the {{jalink|Kamo Asaomi clan|Q122979457|Kamo clan}}, and it is said that the expansion of the Kamo clan into this area is behind <ref name="Gods"/>.
:: In the Jindai volume of "{{jalink|Nihon Shoki|Q813935}}", the main deity of Kotojiro became Yahiro Kumagani and was the daughter of {{jalink|Mishima Noraku||Mishimamizo Hiromimi}}, Mishimazokohime ({{jalink|Tamakushihime|Q115 72681}}), and it is written that {{jalink|Himetatarai Suzuhime|Q5353793|Himetaka Isuzuhime no Mikoto}} was born after {{jalink|Emperor Jimmu|Q200188}}. The {{jalink|Mizokui Shrine|Q11564491}} is enshrined near our company as the guardian deity of the Mishimamizo-Komi clan.The enshrined deity that appears to be classical is written as {{jalink|Engishiki Shinmecho|Q11064932}}, indicating that there was only one main deity. In the 8th century Fudoki of Iyo Province, it is written as ``Oyamazumi-kami'', and in ``{{jalink|Nihonshoki Collection|Q11508272}}'', which was compiled in 1455-57, it is also written as ``Oyamazumi-jin.'' ``{{jalink|Specially Selected Names of Gods|Q11571092}}'', which was published as a commentary on the Engishiki Shinmyocho, also states that it is ``Oyamazumi no Mikoto'', and there is an annotation saying that the theory of Kotoshironushi deity is originally different. However, since the Mishima Kamo Shrine that appears in these documents is located in Shimashita District, and that the Company called it ``Ikushima Daimyojin'' instead of ``Mishima'' before the 17th century, it is possible that this Mishima Kamo Shrine is not the Company's but the {{jalink|Kamo Shrine (Takatsuki City)|Q11675604|Kamo Shrine}} of Ronsha.On the other hand, in documents from the 18th century onwards that can be reliably compared to ours, there is confusion about the deity enshrined. In ``{{jalink|Setyo Gundan|Q11498591}}'' compiled in 1701, Mishima Kamo Shrine in Mishimae Village is described as ``{{jalink|Kamo Kenkakumi no Mikoto|Q116349 39|Kamomiso Okami}}', in the 1725 Yodo River Ryobank List, '{{jalink|Joshiro Nushikami}}', and '{{jalink|Gokinaishi|Q11]' published in 1735-36. 372555}}', 'Oyamazumi no Mikoto', '{{jalink|Settsu Meisho Zue|Q11498549}}' published in 1796-98, 'Kotoshiro Nushigami', '{ In {jalink|Shinja Roku|Q11590708}}, it is written as ``Oyamagigami'' or ``{{jalink|Oyamakuijin|Q10935105}} (Kamomiso Okami).''

== History ==

== Founding ==
According to the shrine's legend, it was founded in the mid-4th century <ref name="History"/>. It is said that our company was originally enshrined on Kawanakajima (Mishima) in {{jalink|Yodogawa|Q1140505}}, and according to the shrine's legend, when {{jalink|Emperor Nintoku|Q313119}} built {{jalink|Ibarada Tsutsumi|Q11617931}}, it was transferred from Baekje and enshrined as the god of guardianship of the Yodogawa River.<ref name="History">[http://www.tcn.zaq.ne.jp/akbus600/rekishi/rekishi.html History] (official website). </ref>.

According to the anecdote from the above-mentioned ``Iyokuni Fudoki,'' Oyamazumi no Kami was enshrined on Mishima Island in Settsu Province from Baekje, and then transferred to Oyamazumi Shrine in Iyo Province. According to the company's biography, the company was spun off into Oyamazumi Shrine in Iyo Province and Izu Mishima Shrine ({{jalink|Mishima Taisha|Q650772}}) in Izu.<ref name="History"/>

On the other hand, it has been pointed out that the Kamo clan, which belongs to the Jigi lineage, has moved into the area, since Kotoshironushi-kami is enshrined as the enshrined deity. According to this theory, the name ``Mishima Kamo Shrine'' was born when Oyamazumi (Mishima), who had already been enshrined as the god of ferryboats on the Yodogawa River, and Kotoshironushi (Kamo) were enshrined together.

== Outline ==
In the national history, "{{jalink|Answers of Three Japanese Dynasties|Q1052981}}" {{jalink|Genkei|Q747451}}8 ({{jalink|884|Q23 895}}) In the December 21st article, there is a description that he bestowed the rank of {{jalink|Divinity|Q11591025}} from the Upper Sixth Rank to the Lower Junior Fifth Rank to ``Mishima no Kami of Settsu Province.'' Also, in "{{jalink|Engishiki Shinmyocho|Q11064932}}" compiled in {{jalink|Extension (era name)|Q1327274|Extension}} 5 years ({{jalink|927|Q30470}}), it is written as "Settsu Province {{jalink|Shimashita County|Q10976940}}" as {{jalink|Shikiuchi Shrine}}. There is a description of ``Mishima Kamo Shrine'', and it is said to be {{jalink|Ronsha|Q135022904}}. However, in all of the above, it is also pointed out that {{jalink|Kamo Shrine (Takatsuki City)|Q11675604|Kamo Shrine}} in Akaoji-cho, Takatsuki City is also mentioned as another non-sha <ref name="place name"/>.Regarding the identification of Shikinai Shrine, our company is located in {{jalink|Shimakami District|Q10965808}}, and Kamo Shrine in Akaoji Town is believed to be located in Shimashita District, and the latter Kamo Shrine seems to be the most likely location for the district. </ref>. In addition, the fact that our company used to be called ``Ikushima Daimyojin'' is one of the reasons for not comparing our company with <ref name="place name"/>. On the other hand, it has been pointed out that Kamo Shrine, which is located far from a river, does not fall under this category, since in the Iyo no Kuni Fudoki Ibibun, another name for Oyamazumi no Kami is ``Watashi (Watashi) God''. </ref>. In any case, it has not yet been determined.

Our company is said to have originally been located on Kawanakajima (Mishima), a sandbar in {{jalink|Yodogawa|Q1140505}}<ref name="History"/>. However, it is said that it was moved to its current location during the construction of the Yodo River embankment in 1598. In {{jalink|Genna (Japan)|Q635245|Genna}}5 ({{jalink|1619|Q6804}}), two stones were donated by {{jalink|Takatsuki clan|Q10863415|Takatsuki clan lord}} and {{jalink|Matsudaira Ienobu|Q5368670}}<ref name="Place name"/>.It entered {{jalink|Meiji|Q3125096}}, and was ranked as {{jalink|Gosha|Q134917316}} in {{jalink|Modern shrine ranking system|Q712534}}. In 1908, surrounding shrines such as Karasaki Shrine and Tenman Shrine were enshrined at <ref name="place name"/>.

== Legend ==
It is said that Emperor Goshirakawa's Chugu {{jalink|Shigeko Taira|Q11061157|Kenshunmonin}} gave birth to Emperor Takakura after praying to our company. In addition, as a token of his gratitude, he commissioned {{jalink|Mishima Shrine (Kyoto City)|Q63147928|Mishima Shrine}} in Kyoto. However, there is a different theory that says that Mishima Shrine in Kyoto was inspired by {{jalink|Mishima Taisha|Q650772}} in Izu.

== Festival ==

* Burning Festival (January 15th)
*Setsubun Festival (February 3rd)
* Spring Festival (April 20th)
* Peace Memorial Ceremony for the War Dead (September)
* Karasaki Shrine Autumn Festival (October 20th and 21st)
* Autumn Festival Yoimiya Festival (4th Saturday of October)
* Autumn Festival (4th Sunday of October)
* Shichigosan Pilgrimage (November 1st-30th)

In ancient times, based on the story in the Jindai section of the Nihon Shoki that Kotoshiro-nushi-kami visited {{jalink|Tamakushihime|Q11572681|Mishimazokahime}}, it is said that the Shinto shrine was held on the same day as Mizokui Shrine, which enshrines Mishimazokahime.<ref name="place name"/>
